sanskrit: mayā mantrabalaṃ jñātum āhūtas tvaṃ vibhāvaso bālyād bāleti kṛtvā tat kṣantum arhasi me vibho
english: O Vibhāvasu, you were summoned by me to test the power of my mantra. Having treated it as a childish act, saying it was mere child's play, you ought to forgive me for that, O mighty one.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca bāleti kṛtvānunayaṃ tavāhaṃ; dadāni nānyānunayaṃ labheta ātmapradānaṃ kuru kuntikanye; śāntis tavaivaṃ hi bhavec ca bhīru
english: Sūrya said: Accepting your plea that it was a childish act, I grant you this concession — no other concession shall be obtained. Give yourself to me, O daughter of Kuntī; only thus will you find peace, O timid one.

sanskrit: na cāpi yuktaṃ gantuṃ hi mayā mithyākṛtena vai gamiṣyāmy anavadyāṅgi loke samavahāsyatām sarveṣāṃ vibudhānāṃ ca vaktavyaḥ syām ahaṃ śubhe
english: Moreover, it is not fitting that I should depart having been summoned falsely. If I go now, O blameless-limbed one, I shall become a laughingstock in the world, and all the gods will have reason to mock me, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ mayā samāgaccha putraṃ lapsyasi mādṛśam viśiṣṭā sarvalokeṣu bhaviṣyasi ca bhāmini
english: Therefore, unite with me; you shall obtain a son equal to me, and you shall become distinguished in all the worlds, O beautiful one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tu kanyā bahuvidhaṃ bruvantī madhuraṃ vacaḥ anunetuṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ na śaśāka manasvinī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But that high-minded maiden, speaking sweet words in many ways, was unable to appease the thousand-rayed one.

sanskrit: na śaśāka yadā bālā pratyākhyātuṃ tamonudam bhītā śāpāt tato rājan dadhyau dīrgham athāntaram
english: When the young girl was unable to refuse the dispeller of darkness, frightened of a curse, O king, she then reflected for a long time.

sanskrit: anāgasaḥ pituḥ śāpo brāhmaṇasya tathaiva ca mannimittaḥ kathaṃ na syāt kruddhād asmād vibhāvasoḥ
english: A curse from an innocent father and likewise from a brahmin — how could I not incur such a curse on account of myself from this wrathful Vibhāvasu?

sanskrit: bālenāpi satā mohād bhṛśaṃ sāpahnavāny api nātyāsādayitavyāni tejāṃsi ca tapāṃsi ca
english: Even by a child, even in confusion, even with the most vehement denials, the fierce energy and austerities of the mighty should not be provoked excessively.

sanskrit: sāham adya bhṛśaṃ bhītā gṛhītā ca kare bhṛśam kathaṃ tv akāryaṃ kuryāṃ vai pradānaṃ hy ātmanaḥ svayam
english: I am now greatly frightened and my hand is firmly seized — yet how can I perform this improper act of surrendering myself on my own?

sanskrit: saivaṃ śāpaparitrastā bahu cintayatī tadā mohenābhiparītāṅgī smayamānā punaḥ punaḥ
english: She, thus terrified of the curse, thinking over many things, her limbs overcome with confusion, smiling again and again—

sanskrit: taṃ devam abravīd bhītā bandhūnāṃ rājasattama vrīḍāvihvalayā vācā śāpatrastā viśāṃ pate
english: — addressed that god, frightened for her kinsmen, O best of kings, with voice trembling in shame, terrified of the curse, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca pitā me dhriyate deva mātā cānye ca bāndhavāḥ na teṣu dhriyamāṇeṣu vidhilopo bhaved ayam
english: Kuntī said: O god, my father lives, as does my mother and other kinsmen. While they are alive, this transgression of custom should not occur.

sanskrit: tvayā me saṃgamo deva yadi syād vidhivarjitaḥ mannimittaṃ kulasyāsya loke kīrtir naśet tataḥ
english: O god, if union with you were to take place outside of proper rites, then on my account the fame of this family would be destroyed in the world.

sanskrit: atha vā dharmam etaṃ tvaṃ manyase tapatāṃ vara ṛte pradānād bandhubhyas tava kāmaṃ karomy aham
english: Or if you, O foremost among the radiant ones, consider this to be righteous even without the gift of myself by my kinsmen, then I shall fulfill your desire.

sanskrit: ātmapradānaṃ durdharṣa tava kṛtvā satī tv aham tvayi dharmo yaśaś caiva kīrtir āyuś ca dehinām
english: Having surrendered myself to you as a chaste woman, O invincible one, may righteousness, fame, glory, and the life-span of embodied beings rest in you.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca na te pitā na te mātā guravo vā śucismite prabhavanti varārohe bhadraṃ te śṛṇu me vacaḥ
english: Sūrya said: Neither your father, nor your mother, nor your teachers have authority over you, O bright-smiling one, O one of beautiful hips. May good come to you — hear my words.

sanskrit: sarvān kāmayate yasmāt kaner dhātoś ca bhāmini tasmāt kanyeha suśroṇi svatantrā varavarṇini
english: Because the root 'kan' and the verbal root from which 'kanya' is derived signifies desiring from all, O beautiful one, therefore a maiden here, O lovely-hipped one, O one of excellent complexion, is independent.

sanskrit: nādharmaś caritaḥ kaś cit tvayā bhavati bhāmini adharmaṃ kuta evāhaṃ careyaṃ lokakāmyayā
english: No unrighteousness whatsoever would be committed by you, O beautiful one. How could I, who am desired by the worlds, ever practice unrighteousness?

sanskrit: anāvṛtāḥ striyaḥ sarvā narāś ca varavarṇini svabhāva eṣa lokānāṃ vikāro 'nya iti smṛtaḥ
english: All women and men are naturally free and unrestrained, O one of excellent complexion — this is the natural order of the worlds; anything else is considered a distortion.

sanskrit: sā mayā saha saṃgamya punaḥ kanyā bhaviṣyasi putraś ca te mahābāhur bhaviṣyati mahāyaśāḥ
english: After uniting with me, you shall again become a virgin, and the son born to you shall be mighty-armed and of great renown.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca yadi putro mama bhavet tvattaḥ sarvatamopaha kuṇḍalī kavacī śūro mahābāhur mahābalaḥ
english: Kuntī said: If a son should be born to me from you, O dispeller of all darkness — one who is adorned with earrings, clad in armor, a hero, mighty-armed, and of great strength—

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca bhaviṣyati mahābāhuḥ kuṇḍalī divyavarmabhṛt ubhayaṃ cāmṛtamayaṃ tasya bhadre bhaviṣyati
english: Sūrya said: He shall be mighty-armed, adorned with earrings, and bearing divine armor; both of these, O auspicious one, shall be made of ambrosia.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca yady etad amṛtād asti kuṇḍale varma cottamam mama putrasya yaṃ vai tvaṃ matta utpādayiṣyasi
english: Kuntī said: If the earrings and the excellent armor of my son, whom you shall beget from yourself upon me, are indeed made of ambrosia—

sanskrit: astu me saṃgamo deva yathoktaṃ bhagavaṃs tvayā tvadvīryarūpasattvaujā dharmayukto bhavet sa ca
english: — then let union with me take place, O god, as you have declared, O blessed one; and may that son be endowed with righteousness, with your valor, beauty, essence, and energy.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca adityā kuṇḍale rājñi datte me mattakāśini te 'sya dāsyāmi vai bhīru varma caivedam uttamam
english: Sūrya said: O queen, the earrings were given to me by Aditi, shining with intoxicating splendor; I shall give both these and this excellent armor to your son, O timid one.

sanskrit: pṛthovāca paramaṃ bhagavan deva saṃgamiṣye tvayā saha yadi putro bhaved evaṃ yathā vadasi gopate
english: Pṛthu said: By all means, O blessed god, I shall unite with you, if a son shall be born as you have described, O lord of rays.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathety uktvā tu tāṃ kuntīm āviveśa vihaṃgamaḥ svarbhānuśatrur yogātmā nābhyāṃ pasparśa caiva tām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying 'so be it,' the sky-traveler, the enemy of Svarbhānu, whose essence is yoga, entered Kuntī and touched her at the navel.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā vihvalevāsīt kanyā sūryasya tejasā papātātha ca sā devī śayane mūḍhacetanā
english: Then that maiden became overwhelmed by the radiance of Sūrya; that divine girl fell upon the bed, her mind bewildered.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca sādhayiṣyāmi suśroṇi putraṃ vai janayiṣyasi sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kanyā caiva bhaviṣyasi
english: Sūrya said: I shall bring it about, O lovely-hipped one — you shall give birth to a son, the foremost among all who bear weapons, and you shall remain a virgin.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sā vrīḍitā bālā tadā sūryam athābravīt evam astv iti rājendra prasthitaṃ bhūrivarcasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then that ashamed young girl spoke to Sūrya as he was departing, O king of kings, saying 'so be it' to the one of great splendor.

sanskrit: iti smoktā kuntirājātmajā sā; vivasvantaṃ yācamānā salajjā tasmin puṇye śayanīye papāta; mohāviṣṭā bhajyamānā lateva
english: Thus addressed, that daughter of the king Kuntī, having beseeched Vivasvat with shame, fell upon that sacred bed, overcome with stupor, like a creeper being broken.

sanskrit: tāṃ tigmāṃśus tejasā mohayitvā; yogenāviṣyātmasaṃsthāṃ cakāra na caivaināṃ dūṣayām āsa bhānuḥ; saṃjñāṃ lebhe bhūya evātha bālā
english: The sharp-rayed one, having stupefied her with his radiance, entered her through yoga and established himself within her; yet the sun did not defile her. The young girl then regained consciousness.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato garbhaḥ samabhavat pṛthāyāḥ pṛthivīpate śukle daśottare pakṣe tārāpatir ivāmbare
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then a child was conceived within Pṛthā, O lord of the earth, in the tenth month of the bright fortnight, like the moon-lord in the sky.

sanskrit: sā bāndhavabhayād bālā taṃ garbhaṃ vinigūhatī dhārayām āsa suśroṇī na caināṃ bubudhe janaḥ
english: That young girl, lovely-hipped, concealing the embryo out of fear of her kinsmen, bore it within herself; no one became aware of her.

sanskrit: na hi tāṃ veda nāry anyā kā cid dhātreyikām ṛte kanyāpuragatāṃ bālāṃ nipuṇāṃ parirakṣaṇe
english: Indeed, no other woman knew of her, except the nurse who was skilled in guarding secrets, residing in the women's quarters.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena sā garbhaṃ suṣuve varavarṇinī kanyaiva tasya devasya prasādād amaraprabham
english: Then in time that one of excellent complexion gave birth to the child, still a virgin, by the grace of that god — a child of divine brilliance.

sanskrit: tathaiva baddhakavacaṃ kanakojjvalakuṇḍalam haryakṣaṃ vṛṣabhaskandhaṃ yathāsya pitaraṃ tathā
english: And just so — clad in natural armor, adorned with golden gleaming earrings, with tawny eyes and the shoulders of a bull, just like his father.

sanskrit: jātamātraṃ ca taṃ garbhaṃ dhātryā saṃmantrya bhāminī mañjūṣāyām avadadhe svāstīrṇāyāṃ samantataḥ
english: As soon as the child was born, that beautiful woman, after consulting with the nurse, placed him in a box that was well-lined on all sides.

sanskrit: madhūcchiṣṭasthitāyāṃ sā sukhāyāṃ rudatī tathā ślakṣṇāyāṃ supidhānāyām aśvanadyām avāsṛjat
english: In that box coated with beeswax, comfortable, smooth, well-covered — weeping — she set it afloat on the Aśva river.

sanskrit: jānatī cāpy akartavyaṃ kanyāyā garbhadhāraṇam putrasnehena rājendra karuṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: Knowing full well that bearing a child while an unwed maiden was improper, yet out of love for her son, O king of kings, she lamented piteously.

sanskrit: samutsṛjantī mañjūṣām aśvanadyās tadā jale uvāca rudatī kuntī yāni vākyāni tac chṛṇu
english: As she was releasing the box into the waters of the Aśva river, weeping, Kuntī spoke these words — hear them.

sanskrit: svasti te 'stv āntarikṣebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaś ca putraka divyebhyaś caiva bhūtebhyas tathā toyacarāś ca ye
english: May you be blessed by the beings of the atmosphere, by those of the earth, O my little son; and by the divine beings and those who move through water.

sanskrit: śivās te santu panthāno mā ca te paripanthinaḥ āgamāś ca tathā putra bhavantv adrohacetasaḥ
english: May your paths be auspicious and free from adversaries; and may those you encounter, O son, be of benevolent hearts.

sanskrit: pātu tvāṃ varuṇo rājā salile salileśvaraḥ antarikṣe 'ntarikṣasthaḥ pavanaḥ sarvagas tathā
english: May King Varuṇa, the lord of waters, protect you in the water; may Pavana, who dwells in the atmosphere and moves everywhere, protect you in the sky.

sanskrit: pitā tvāṃ pātu sarvatra tapanas tapatāṃ varaḥ yena datto 'si me putra divyena vidhinā kila
english: May your father, the sun, the foremost among the radiant ones, protect you everywhere — by whom you were given to me, O son, truly by a divine ordinance.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyā viśve ca devatāḥ marutaś ca sahendreṇa diśaś ca sadigīśvarāḥ
english: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, the Vishvadevas, the Maruts together with Indra, and the directions with their guardian lords—

sanskrit: rakṣantu tvāṃ surāḥ sarve sameṣu viṣameṣu ca vetsyāmi tvāṃ videśe 'pi kavacenopasūcitam
english: — may all the gods protect you on level ground and in rough places alike. Even in a foreign land I shall recognize you by your armor.

sanskrit: dhanyas te putra janako devo bhānur vibhāvasuḥ yas tvāṃ drakṣyati divyena cakṣuṣā vāhinīgatam
english: Blessed is your father, the god Bhānu, the glorious Vibhāvasu, who shall behold you in the army with his divine eye.

sanskrit: dhanyā sā pramadā yā tvāṃ putratve kalpayiṣyati yasyās tvaṃ tṛṣitaḥ putra stanaṃ pāsyasi devaja
english: Blessed is that woman who shall accept you as her son, at whose breast you, thirsting, O son, shall suckle, O god-born one.

sanskrit: ko nu svapnas tayā dṛṣṭo yā tvām ādityavarcasam divyavarmasamāyuktaṃ divyakuṇḍalabhūṣitam
english: What a dream must she have seen, she who shall accept as her son you — brilliant as the sun, clad in divine armor, adorned with divine earrings—

sanskrit: padmāyataviśālākṣaṃ padmatāmratalojjvalam sulalāṭaṃ sukeśāntaṃ putratve kalpayiṣyati
english: — with eyes long and wide as lotuses, with palms and soles glowing like copper lotuses, with a fine forehead and beautiful hair — she who shall accept you as her son.

sanskrit: dhanyā drakṣyanti putra tvāṃ bhūmau saṃsarpamāṇakam avyaktakalavākyāni vadantaṃ reṇuguṇṭhitam
english: Blessed will those be who shall see you, O son, crawling upon the ground, speaking indistinct babbling words, covered in dust.

sanskrit: dhanyā drakṣyanti putra tvāṃ punar yauvanage mukhe himavadvanasaṃbhūtaṃ siṃhaṃ kesariṇaṃ yathā
english: Blessed will those be who shall again see you, O son, when you reach the bloom of youth, like a maned lion born in the forests of the Himālayas.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ rājan vilapya karuṇaṃ pṛthā avāsṛjata mañjūṣām aśvanadyās tadā jale
english: Having thus lamented in many ways, O king, Pṛthā released the box into the waters of the Aśva river at that time.

sanskrit: rudatī putraśokārtā niśīthe kamalekṣaṇā dhātryā saha pṛthā rājan putradarśanalālasā
english: Weeping, afflicted with grief for her son, at midnight, lotus-eyed Pṛthā, together with her nurse, O king, longing to see her son—

sanskrit: visarjayitvā mañjūṣāṃ saṃbodhanabhayāt pituḥ viveśa rājabhavanaṃ punaḥ śokāturā tataḥ
english: — having released the box, fearing discovery by her father, re-entered the royal palace, then overcome with grief.

sanskrit: mañjūṣā tv aśvanadyāḥ sā yayau carmaṇvatīṃ nadīm carmaṇvatyāś ca yamunāṃ tato gaṅgāṃ jagāma ha
english: That box from the Aśva river went to the Carmaṇvatī river, and from the Carmaṇvatī it went to the Yamunā, and then it reached the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāḥ sūtaviṣayaṃ campām abhyāyayau purīm sa mañjūṣāgato garbhas taraṅgair uhyamānakaḥ
english: From the Gaṅgā, borne along by the waves, the child in the box approached the city of Campā in the territory of the Sutas.

sanskrit: amṛtād utthitaṃ divyaṃ tat tu varma sakuṇḍalam dhārayām āsa taṃ garbhaṃ daivaṃ ca vidhinirmitam
english: That divine armor with the earrings, born of ambrosia, bore up the child — that divine being fashioned by fate.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu dhṛtarāṣṭrasya vai sakhā sūto 'dhiratha ity eva sadāro jāhnavīṃ yayau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At that very time, a friend of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the charioteer known as Adhiratha, together with his wife went to the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā).

sanskrit: tasya bhāryābhavad rājan rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi rādhā nāma mahābhāgā na sā putram avindata apatyārthe paraṃ yatnam akaroc ca viśeṣataḥ
english: His wife, O king, was unrivaled in beauty upon the earth — the greatly fortunate Rādhā by name. She had not obtained a son, and she had made every special effort for the sake of offspring.

sanskrit: sā dadarśātha mañjūṣām uhyamānāṃ yadṛcchayā dattarakṣāpratisarām anvālabhanaśobhitām ūrmītaraṅgair jāhnavyāḥ samānītām upahvaram
english: She then saw a box being carried along by chance, adorned with protective charms, beautiful with decorative touches, brought to a secluded spot by the waves of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: sā tāṃ kautūhalāt prāptāṃ grāhayām āsa bhāminī tato nivedayām āsa sūtasyādhirathasya vai
english: That beautiful woman, out of curiosity, had it pulled in and retrieved; then she informed the charioteer Adhiratha.

sanskrit: sa tām uddhṛtya mañjūṣām utsārya jalam antikāt yantrair udghāṭayām āsa so 'paśyat tatra bālakam
english: He lifted out the box, cleared the water from nearby, opened it with implements, and saw therein a baby boy.

sanskrit: taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ hemavarmadharaṃ tathā mṛṣṭakuṇḍalayuktena vadanena virājatā
english: — resplendent like the young sun, clad in golden armor, radiant with a face adorned with gleaming earrings.

sanskrit: sa sūto bhāryayā sārdhaṃ vismayotphullalocanaḥ aṅkam āropya taṃ bālaṃ bhāryāṃ vacanam abravīt
english: The charioteer, his eyes wide open in wonder, together with his wife, lifting the infant into his lap, spoke these words to his wife.

sanskrit: idam atyadbhutaṃ bhīru yato jāto 'smi bhāmini dṛṣṭavān devagarbho 'yaṃ manye 'smān samupāgataḥ
english: This is most wondrous, O timid one, from where I was born, O beautiful one. I believe this child of divine womb has come to us.

sanskrit: anapatyasya putro 'yaṃ devair datto dhruvaṃ mama ity uktvā taṃ dadau putraṃ rādhāyai sa mahīpate
english: Saying 'This son has surely been given to me, who am childless, by the gods,' he gave the son to Rādhā, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha taṃ rādhā vidhivad divyarūpiṇam putraṃ kamalagarbhābhaṃ devagarbhaṃ śriyā vṛtam
english: Rādhā accepted him according to proper rites — that one of divine form, the son radiant as the interior of a lotus, the divine child endowed with glory.

sanskrit: pupoṣa cainaṃ vidhivad vavṛdhe sa ca vīryavān tataḥ prabhṛti cāpy anye prābhavann aurasāḥ sutāḥ
english: She nurtured him properly, and he grew up full of valor. From that time on, other natural sons were also born to them.

sanskrit: vasuvarmadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ bālaṃ hemakuṇḍalam nāmāsya vasuṣeṇeti tataś cakrur dvijātayaḥ
english: Seeing that infant bearing the armor of the Vasus and golden earrings, the twice-born thereafter gave him the name Vasushena.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa sūtaputratvaṃ jagāmāmitavikramaḥ vasuṣeṇa iti khyāto vṛṣa ity eva ca prabhuḥ
english: Thus that one of immeasurable valor came to be known as the son of a charioteer — renowned as Vasushena and also as Vrisha, the lord.

sanskrit: sa jyeṣṭhaputraḥ sūtasya vavṛdhe 'ṅgeṣu vīryavān cāreṇa viditaś cāsīt pṛthāyā divyavarmabhṛt
english: He, the eldest son of the charioteer, grew up with valor in Aṅga; and he was recognized by spies as Pṛthā's son, bearing divine armor.

sanskrit: sūtas tv adhirathaḥ putraṃ vivṛddhaṃ samaye tataḥ dṛṣṭvā prasthāpayām āsa puraṃ vāraṇasāhvayam
english: The charioteer Adhiratha, seeing his son fully grown in due time, then sent him to the city named Varanasahvaya (Hāstinapura).

sanskrit: tatropasadanaṃ cakre droṇasyeṣvastrakarmaṇi sakhyaṃ duryodhanenaivam agacchat sa ca vīryavān
english: There he attended upon Droṇa in the training of bow-craft and the art of weapons, and that valorous one also formed a friendship with Duryodhana.

sanskrit: droṇāt kṛpāc ca rāmāc ca so 'stragrāmaṃ caturvidham labdhvā loke 'bhavat khyātaḥ parameṣvāsatāṃ gataḥ
english: Having obtained the fourfold arsenal of weapons from Droṇa, Kṛpa, and Rāma (Parashurama), he became famous in the world and attained the status of the greatest archers.

sanskrit: saṃdhāya dhārtarāṣṭreṇa pārthānāṃ vipriye sthitaḥ yoddhum āśaṃsate nityaṃ phalgunena mahātmanā
english: Allying with the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and standing against the Pārthas, he ever desired to fight with the great-souled Phalguna (Arjuna).

sanskrit: sadā hi tasya spardhāsīd arjunena viśāṃ pate arjunasya ca karṇena yato dṛṣṭo babhūva saḥ
english: For there was always rivalry between him and Arjuna, O lord of the people, and between Arjuna and Karṇa — from the time they first laid eyes on each other.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kuṇḍalinaṃ dṛṣṭvā varmaṇā ca samanvitam avadhyaṃ samare matvā paryatapyad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: But seeing him adorned with earrings and clad in armor, and deeming him invincible in battle, Yudhiṣṭhira was greatly tormented.

sanskrit: yadā tu karṇo rājendra bhānumantaṃ divākaram stauti madhyaṃdine prāpte prāñjaliḥ salile sthitaḥ
english: But when Karṇa, O king of kings, stands in the water with joined palms at midday, praising the radiant sun, the day-maker—
